newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil '97 budget sees 0.8 pct GDP primary surplus.
newsitem.headline: Brazil '97 budget sees 0.8 pct GDP primary surplus.

text.p: Planning Minister Antonio Kandir on Friday sent the 1997 budget to Congress, predicting a primary surplus of 0.8 percent of Gross Domestic Product, up from an estimated 0.59 percent in 1996.
Kandir said he expected inflation in 1997 to be around 10 percent.

The 176 billion real budget, which foresees 15 billion reais in investment by state-owned companies, sets the 1997 federal government operational deficit at 1.07 percent of GDP, versus an estimated 1.38 percent in 1996.
Kandir said debt servicing costs in 1997 were expected to rise to 15.548 billion reais from an estimated 14.359 billion in 1996.
He said that despite the growth in debt-servicing costs, there would be an improvement in the primary result which would lead to a "significant" reduction in the operational deficit.
A breakdown of the budget showed 1997 receipts of 177.2 billion reais, with total expenditure at 174.9 billion reais.

Federal government payroll costs are to rise to 45.04 billion reais in 1997 from 39.7 billion in 1996, although the 1997 figure represented 5.42 percent of GDP, down from an estimated 5.46 percent in 1996.
